text:
Liam O'Brien's job hasn't changed in years: play eight minutes, finish every check, and answer the door when someone knocks. Utah fans call him "Spicy Tuna," and through nine games he has 38 hits and six shots on goal. That ratio tells you the role.

There are no points yet, and our numbers didn't expect many. He has generated 1.14 expected goals (the quality of his chances) all season, close to his usual rate. The surprise is what happens around him: at five on five, Utah has taken 59% of the expected goals with him on the ice. In about eight minutes a night over nine games, that's a sample we wouldn't lean on, but his shifts haven't been a liability.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says he carries the puck in on only 27% of his entries, so his line lives on dump-ins and the forecheck, which suits an undrafted 6'1", 215-pound winger out of the QMJHL. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season. Watch the minutes: they've slipped by more than a minute a night lately, and Utah has won one of the nine games he's played.
